bib.title: Cognitive Foundations for Reasoning and Their Manifestation in LLMs

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Cognitive Foundations for Reasoning and Their Manifestation in LLMs", Kargupta, Li, Wang, Lee, Chen, Ahia, Light, Griffiths, Kleiman-Weiner, Han, Celikyilmaz, Tsvetkov. arXiv 2511.16660v2, 24 Nov 2025, preprint.

COVERAGE: All 40 pages, 165,028 of 165,028 chars (extraction at /tmp/kg.txt, 2100 lines). The reference list was skimmed only for origins. Annotation prompts for the other 27 elements are in the authors' repo, not the PDF.

CENTRAL CLAIM: 16 open-weight reasoning models do not deploy the reasoning behaviors that predict success, and the gap is widest on ill-structured problems. A test-time prompt that spells out the successful behavior sequence helps capable models on ill-structured tasks. It hurts small ones.

IMPORTANT FOR THE TARGET NOTE: the paper never uses the terms overthinking or underthinking. It does not vary thinking budget, token limits, or thinking on versus off. Its only intervention is structured guidance in the prompt. Its nearest link to your topic is that reasoning trace length differs by problem type, and the prompting finding below.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Structured guidance helps capable models on ill-structured problems and hurts weak ones. Average change is only +2.0%.
 number: up to +66.7%. Average across 14 models is +2.0%. Per problem type the averages are Diag +22.9, Case +26.7, Dilemma +21.4, Fact +16.3, Rule +12.9, Algo +1.1, Story +2.4, Log +3.3.
 setup: about 50 text problems per model and problem type, half previously correct and half previously wrong. Metric is relative percent change in accuracy, (after-before)/before. Guidance is an auto-generated prompt built from a 7-node consensus graph of the successful behavior sequence for that problem type. 14 models in Table 4. Accuracy was judged by AlpacaEval with GPT-4o as judge.
 quote: "Test-time reasoning guidance improves performance by up to 66.7% on ill-structured problems while maintaining baseline performance on well-structured ones."
 where: p.4 (intro) and Table 4, p.20
 Caution: the "maintaining baseline on well-structured" wording is looser than Table 4. Algo is +1.1% on average, but individual models fall as low as -87.0 (Story, DeepScaleR) and -72.0 (Algo, Hermes-3).
2. A capability threshold. Small or weak models degrade sharply under the scaffold.
 number: DeepScaleR-1.5B averages -52.6%. Hermes-3-Llama-3-8B averages -17.5%. Both show -72.0 on one problem type (DeepScaleR on Story -87.0, Hermes on Algo -72.0). Strong models gain: Qwen3-14B +22.5, R1-Distill-Qwen-32B +22.3, R1-Distill-Llama-70B +21.9, Qwen3-32B +14.8, Qwen3-8B +13.8.
 quote: "Smaller or less capable models, particularly Hermes-3-Llama-3-8B and DeepScaleR-1.5B, show pronounced performance degradationacross most problem types, with losses exceeding 50% in several categories (e.g., -72.0% for both on algorithmic problems)."
 The paper's reading: "models must possess sufficient reasoning flexibility and instruction-following ability to productively adapt their processes to detailed structural guidance."
 where: p.20-21
 Caveat: the text says -72.0% for both on algorithmic. Table 4 shows DeepScaleR Algo -56.0 and Hermes Algo -72.0.
3. Design problems collapsed under the scaffold.
 quote (table caption): "Design problems showed catastrophic failure (0% accuracy) across all models after steering and are excluded."
 where: Table 4 caption, p.20
 The text does not explain this. The headline numbers therefore exclude the worst case.
4. Models narrow their repertoire on ill-structured problems, which is the opposite of what success needs.
 number: mean element presence is 0.397±0.255 on well-structured types (algorithmic, story, rule-using) and 0.337±0.261 on ill-structured (case analysis, design, dilemma). Mean PPMI with success is 0.046±0.063 on well-structured and 0.186±0.114 on diagnosis-solution through dilemma.
 setup: 192,709 traces, 18 models, text, audio and image. Elements annotated at span level by GPT-4.1 at temperature 0.6. Problems typed with Jonassen (2000) typology by majority vote of GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro and Claude-Sonnet-4.5.
 quote: "models have learned to apply their most diverse cognitive elements where they are the least necessary,while defaulting to limited, inflexible strategies precisely where adaptability matters most."
 where: p.15
5. Common reasoning rushes into forward chaining. Successful reasoning scopes the problem first.
 number: on diagnosis problems the common pattern goes straight to forward chaining (Prob 0.748). The successful pattern is selective attention, then sequential organization, then knowledge alignment, then forward chaining. On algorithmic problems the common pattern contains self-awareness (NPMI -0.141) and backtracking (NPMI -0.050), which correlate with failure.
 quote: "The common pattern bypasses this scoping phase entirely, immediately rushing into forward chaining (Prob: 0.748)."
 where: p.18, Figure 6
 Correlational (NPMI of element or edge with correctness), not causal.
6. Prevalence is not the same as usefulness.
 number: logical coherence is present in 91% of traces with average PPMI 0.091. Knowledge alignment has PPMI 0.234 but is in only 20.2% of traces. Evaluation is present in 53.5% with PPMI 0.031. Spatial organization is present in 9.8% with PPMI 0.252.
 quote: "the average PPMI of logical coherence is0.091, despite having a presence rate of91%."
 where: p.16
 The authors say models try to find inconsistencies but "consistently fail to recognize or effectively respond to them".
7. Models repeat verification and backtracking on ground already covered, versus humans.
 number: humans show strongly present self-awareness in 49% of traces versus 19% for LLMs, and abstraction in 54% versus 36%.
 setup: 30 manually annotated traces, humans (educated adults, think-aloud, 18 participants, 54 traces collected) versus LLMs, a small qualitative sample.
 quote: "Human traces exhibit significantly higher strongly present rates of abstract cognitive elements, such as self-awareness (49%vs.19%) and abstraction (54%vs.36%)."
 where: p.19
 Case in Table 3 (checkerboard-domino logical problem): human 166 tokens, DeepSeek-R1 7,632 tokens, with R1 enumerating and re-checking. Design problem: human 2,071 tokens, R1 747 tokens. So R1 is longer on the logical problem and shorter on the design problem. This is a single case, not a measured rate.
8. Trace length and diversity vary by model and problem type.
 number: s1.1-32B has 59.7% mean element presence and 13,210 average characters. Olmo-3-7B-Think is quoted as 48.4% presence and 17,416 average characters, but the Figure 5 caption lists Olmo-3-7B-Think as 0.491. Well-structured problems get longer traces.
 quote: "we observe that well-structured problems feature longer reasoning traces."
 where: p.17
 The authors give two untested hypotheses for why.
9. Accuracy falls as problems get less structured, with exceptions.
 number: story 79.5% (appendix; the main text says 78.8%), algorithmic 63.8%, design 46.6%, diagnosis-solution 44.7%, dilemma 82.4%. Dilemma ranges from 3.2% to 99.1% across models. R1-671B averages 88.0%, Qwen3-32B 81.3%, OpenThinker-32B 75.8%, and DeepScaleR-1.5B 21.6%.
 setup: 16 text models. Ground truth is the reference for verifiable tasks. For non-verifiable tasks the reference is Claude-Sonnet-4.5's own answer.
 where: Table 5/6, p.39
 Dilemma accuracy is graded against a model's answer, so its high scores are weak evidence.
10. The research literature is lopsided.
 number: of 1,598 arXiv papers, decomposition 60%, sequential organization 54-55%, self-awareness 16%, spatial organization 10%.
 quote: "55% examine sequential organization (e.g., reasoning step-by-step), while only 8% study backward chaining"
 where: p.3 and p.21
 Annotated by GPT-4.1 with moderate agreement (ICC 0.593).

LIMITS (stated or visible)
- The authors concede it is unclear whether the guidance "enables genuine deployment of latent capabilities or simply helps models retrieve cached reasoning patterns from training data" (p.22). They call the evidence "strong preliminary".
- The guidance needs prior knowledge of per-problem-type successful patterns. Problem type must be known or classified first.
- All behavior-success links are correlational (NPMI/PPMI). Annotation is by GPT-4.1 only, validated on the small human set.
- Only transformer LMs were studied, so training or architecture causes are not isolated.
- Guidance results cover about 50 text problems per cell, so single cells are noisy. They are percent-relative changes, so a low baseline inflates them. Design is excluded after 0% accuracy. Hermes-3 and DeepScaleR are mostly broken by the scaffold.
- Humans are a small group of educated adults. Audio and image were not part of the guidance test.
- There is no comparison against simple generic prompts such as "think step by step" or a plain strategy hint. The effect of structure versus extra instruction length is not separated.
- The paper has no thinking-budget study, no effort-level study, and no overthinking/underthinking measure.
- Dataset bias: 59% of problems are algorithmic, strategic performance has 0 instances, and creative/expressive has 7. GeneralThought is mostly verifiable tasks. Dilemma data comes from 290 ClaimSpect claims. The models are 2025-era open-weight reasoning models. Frontier closed models were excluded because their traces are summarized.

BUILDS ON
Jonassen (2000) problem typology; Marr (1982) levels of analysis; Fodor (1975) and Fodor & Pylyshyn (1988); Johnson-Laird (1983); Sweller (1988/2011); Newell et al. (1959) and Newell & Simon (1972); Gentner (1983); Gick & Holyoak (1980); Flavell (1979); Nelson (1990). LLM side: Gandhi et al. (2025) on verification, subgoal setting, backtracking and backward chaining as RL-induced behaviors; Wei et al. (2022b), Kojima et al. (2023), Wang et al. (2022), Yao et al. (2023) on CoT prompting, which "elicit latent but not spontaneous behaviors"; Lightman et al. (2023) and Uesato et al. (2022) on process supervision; Lambert et al. (2024); Lanham et al. (2023) and Turpin et al. (2023) on CoT unfaithfulness; Marjanovic et al. (2025) on self-monitoring. Evaluation uses AlpacaEval (Dubois et al., 2024).

CODE
None in the PDF. Code is at github.com/pkargupta/cognitive_foundations, and the annotation prompts are in the repo (the abstraction rubric is in the appendix, p.36). The guidance prompts are said to be "examples provided in our codebase". The guidance-prompt text is not printed in the paper.

FIGURES
- Table 4 (p.20). Per-model by problem-type percent change after cognitive-structure guidance. It is the one place that shows the scaffold helping strong models and hurting weak ones, and it is the most relevant to prompting. Use it for the target note.
- Figure 6 (p.18), "Successful vs. Common 7-node behavioral pattern across all Algorithmic and Diagnosis-Solution reasoning trace with the correlation to success (NPMI) and the probability of each node." It shows how the successful sequence (scope first, align domain knowledge, then forward chaining) differs from the common rush-to-solution sequence, which is what the scaffold prompts encode.
- Also useful: Figure 4 (p.16), which compares element presence with PPMI with success per problem type.

NOTE-SECTION FIT
Best fit is "structure vs free reasoning": prescribed reasoning structure helps strong reasoning models on ill-structured tasks and hurts small ones. It also gives the "when to let them think" angle that scaffolds should be matched to problem structure. It does not support overthinking or underthinking claims.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions in the PDF. Extraction was clean text, although figure and heatmap labels came out as scrambled lists.
- Inconsistencies in the paper itself. (a) The abstract and text cite "Qwen3-7B" on diagnosis (+66.7%), but Table 4 has no Qwen3-7B. The +66.7 appears for R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on Diagnosis. (b) The text gives 170K traces in one place and 192K in another (the text-model total is 169,792 and the grand total is 192,709). (c) Story accuracy is 78.8% in the main text and 79.5% in the appendix. (d) Olmo-3-7B-Think presence is quoted as 48.4% in the text and 0.491 in the Figure 5 caption. (e) The text says "-72.0% for both on algorithmic" but the table shows -56.0 for DeepScaleR. (f) p.23 says meta-cognitive monitoring appears in "8% of reasoning traces and 8% of papers", while elsewhere self-awareness is 16% and evaluation 8%.
- Figure and caption text was read from the extraction. I did not run the figure-caption script or view images.
